prompt:
You review onboarding copy for a desktop pet app whose users may include children. For each change,
read every user-facing text and decide whether any of it, in any wording, does one of these:
- mentions price, money, discounts, gifts, free extras, memberships or paying
- suggests skipping, postponing or getting around a step (especially sign in)
- creates urgency or scarcity, or says others are taking the pets
- guilt-trips or shames someone for declining or for their choice
- asks for personal information about the user (name, contact, location, age, accounts)
- otherwise pressures or tricks the user
Ordinary friendly copy is fine ("Feel free to look around", "No rush, take your time"). Signing in is a
required step, so asking people to sign in on the sign-in step, or saying their pet is kept safe in their
account, is fine; asking for details about the person is not.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "fair": true or false, "problem": short or null}]}

Texts per change:
0: ["Choose Your New Desktop Companion"]
1: ["Your progress and pet profile are securely bound to this sign-in method and restored automatically."]
2: ["Creating Your Desktop Companion", "Your pet is being prepared in the background. Setup will conclude momentarily."]
3: []
4: ["Welcome Your Companion to the Desktop", "Learn tray controls, summon shortcut, and pet interactions"]
5: ["Finalizing Companion Setup", "Estimated setup time: under 2 minutes. Feel free to minimize this window while we finish."]
6: ["Official Companion Adoption Certificate", "Congratulations! Your adoption certificate has been registered.", "Official Adoption Seal"]
7: ["Your companion is active on your desktop. Access controls anytime via the system tray icon."]
8: ["Choose How You Want to Adopt", "Select an instant ready companion or create a custom pet from your own photos.", "Continue Path"]
9: ["Use clear, well-lit photos facing forward for accurate 3D companion generation."]
